tone_statements.citation: Chai, Yuan, Adrián Fernández & Briseida Mendez. 2024. The role of phonation and tone in TAM in Yateé Zapotec. Paper presented at the Annual Meeting of the Society for the Study of the Indigenous Languages of the Americas (SSILA), January 2024. 2-page abstract (slides also posted: file/).
tone_statements.quote: Yateé Zapotec has four tones: High (V́), Low (V̀), Rising (V̌), and Falling (V̂); and three phonations: Modal (V), Checked (Vˀ), and Rearticulated (VˀV). Each phonation can bear any of the four tones (Example 1). ... if the person marker has the same vowel quality as the final vowel in the verb stem, a tonal change occurs (5f vs. 5g: The tone on /a͡u/ changed from low to falling). ... when the imperatives and the past tense cannot be distinguished by phonation, a tone change is observed, suggesting that tone be used with a grammatical function in the language.
tone_statements.locator: abstract p.1 (para. 2, Example 1) and p.2 (final paragraph)
tone_statements.summary: Four tones (High, Low, Rising, Falling) marked on vowels, fully crossed with modal/checked/rearticulated phonation; tone also functions grammatically in TAM/person marking (low -> falling alternation distinguishing imperative vs past with certain person markers); no stress statement.

tone_statements.citation: Chai, Yuan, Adrian Fernández & Briseida Mendez. 2023. Acoustics of the creaky phonations in Yateé Zapotec. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 153(3, Supplement): A296 (meeting abstract, 184th ASA Meeting, Chicago; poster PDF on first author's site: file/).
tone_statements.quote: • Yateé Zapotec (YZ): • Otomanguean:Northern Core Zapotec • Spoken in San Francisco Yateé, Oaxaca, Mexico (~150 speakers), and by diaspora community in Los Angeles. • Existing documentations are on the consonants of YZ [1,2] • Four tones: o Low (V̀), High (V́), Rising (V̌), Falling (V̂) • Three phonations: o Modal V, Rearticulated VˀV, Checked Vˀ ... Mean F0 (Hz) ... Tone Low Falling High Rising ... Pitch track based on modal tokens

tone_statements.citation: Chai, Yuan, Adrián Fernández & Briseida Mendez. 2023. Phonetics of glottalized phonations in Yateé Zapotec. In Radek Skarnitzl & Jan Volín (eds.), Proceedings of the 20th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences (ICPhS 2023, Prague, 7-11 August 2023), paper ID 270 (5 pp.). Prague: Guarant International.
tone_statements.quote: Yateé Zapotec has four tones: low, high, rising, and falling. The four tones are fully crossed with the three phonations. Examples of the interaction between phonation and tone are in Table 1. ... Low tone and falling tone both have a falling contour. Falling tone has a larger falling slope than low tone. High tone and rising tone both have a rising contour. Rising tone has a larger rising slope than high tone. ... phonation is fully crossed with all four tones in the language. A constant f0 is required to maintain the tonal contrast.
tone_statements.locator: p.1 sec. 1 Introduction (with Table 1); p.2 sec. 3 Results (f0); p.4 sec. 4 Discussion and conclusion
tone_statements.summary: Four contrastive tones on the vowel/syllable: Low, High, Rising, Falling (two level, two contour), each combinable with modal, rearticulated (VˀV) and checked (Vˀ) phonation (12 tone-phonation cells attested); phonetically L and F are falling contours (F steeper), H and R rising contours (R steeper); no downstep, sandhi or stress discussed.

sources.note: Appendix entry 'Yatee [JAEGER and VAN VALIN 1982] (19C+ʔ, 4V)' on p.202 lists fortis/lenis consonants, vowels i e a o (plain and checked), 'Tones: high, low, low-to-high rising, high-to-low falling', loan phonemes; no stress/accent line for Yatee (other entries in the same appendix do carry 'Stress is phonemic' / 'Accent falls on the penultimate' lines when the source gives one). Tone survey p.55 lists 'Zapotec (Yatee, Juarez: rising, falling)' under three tones plus combinations. Second-hand and silent on stress.

sources.note: Overview of the suprasegmental system: four tones H, L, R, F and three phonations, every tone-phonation combination attested on /a/; TAM marked by prefixes/suffixes plus phonation and tone; vowel coalescence with person markers changes phonation (modal->checked, checked->rearticulated) and, when phonation cannot distinguish imperative from past, a tone change (e.g. low -> falling) does, i.e. tone has a grammatical function.

Examples of the interaction between phonation and tone are in Table 1. ... Low tone and falling tone both have a falling contour. Falling tone has a larger falling slope than low tone. sources.note: Four lexical tones (low, high, rising, falling) fully crossed with three phonation types (modal, rearticulated VˀV, checked Vˀ); Table 1 gives tone x phonation example words; GAM-fitted f0 contours per tone (low and falling both fall, falling steeper; high and rising both rise, rising steeper); concludes a constant f0 is required to maintain the tonal contrast so f0 is not a phonation cue. No statement on word stress.

tone.quote: We conducted an identification task, providing the participants with five options of words varying in the phonation and tone. The tone are either high or rising tone. The f0 of the stimuli is kept constant at the value and contour in the middle of the high and rising tone.
